summary: Replace the placeholder worker with a supervised production runtime for PostgreSQL leases, transactional outbox to Kafka, durable webhook delivery, reconciliation execution and optional upload-security processing.

impacts.evidence: Cross-tenant discovery is restricted to SECURITY DEFINER lease functions returning only organization/workspace/item identities; every domain repository operation re-enters the returned tenant scope under forced RLS.
Worker logs use bounded machine codes and opaque IDs; secrets remain callback-scoped through SecretProvider and upload bytes remain in quarantine until the existing security decision permits release.
No REST path, OpenAPI operation or response contract changes.
A concrete Kafka adapter now transports the existing canonical event envelope and retry/DLQ headers; event names and schemas are unchanged and worker defaults cover every catalog transport topic.
Connector SDK interfaces and manifests are unchanged; the runtime consumes only the existing account, manifest and Runtime boundaries.
Expand migration 000067 adds a forced-RLS runtime lease table plus narrowly scoped SECURITY DEFINER claim/list/release/complete functions without changing domain table contracts.

Startup composes encrypted secrets, idempotent all-ISR Kafka production, server-derived S3 keys, digest verification and fail-closed ClamAV dependency handling; the sanitized source archive excludes local credentials.
Reconciliation uses an empty ActionPolicy by default, so drift detection cannot automatically perform writes; missing provider source bridges are retried rather than treated as success.
Transactional outbox IDs remain the canonical event identity and upload security mutations retain causation and immutable evidence through the existing repositories.
Durable runtime leases, deterministic reconciliation run IDs from the scheduler, existing outbox identity and bounded retry delays preserve at-least-once execution without claiming false completion.
Kafka events now enter the existing durable webhook service and signed delivery worker; endpoints remain subject to the existing endpoint policy, secret lookup, leases and retry backoff.
Supervisor/component lifecycle, deferred reconciliation and upload outcomes emit stable structured event names and machine error codes.

The worker is additive behind existing process deployment; upload scanning is opt-in, migration 000067 is expand-only, and shared cancellation joins every component before bootstrap shutdown completes.

Targeted tests cover supervisor cancellation/failure, event-catalog topic parity, worker config, bounded S3 quarantine promotion and fail-closed digest handling; repository deployment and supply-chain policy checks pass.
